Al-Masharif Jurnal Ilmu Ekonomi dan Keislaman

Abstrak Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui peluang dan tantangan fintech dalam industri Perbankan Syari'ah di tengah Pandemi. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode deskriftif kualitatif yaitu menelaah sumber-sumber tertulis seperti jurnal, buku, literature, ensiklopedia, karya ilmuan serta berbagai sumber lain baik dalam bentuk tulisan maupun dalam format digital yang relevan. Adapun objek kajian dalam penelitian ini adalah berupa teks-teks atau tulisan-tulisan yang menggambarkan dan memaparkan tentang peluang dan tantangan fintech pada industri perbankan syariah di tengah pandemi Covid-19. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pandemi covid-19 telah memberikan peluang yang lebih besar bagi fintech perbankan syariah disebabkan pandemi telah mendorong masyarakat melakukan transaksi e-comerce. Dimana volume transaksi digital banking meningkat selama pandemi hingga 20,8% yaitu mencapai 1.493 juta kali transaksi dan secara nominal meningkat 23% yaitu mencapai Rp.8.223 triliun. Adapun tantangannya adalah keamanan data dan transaksi pengguna layanan fintech, mudahnya nasabah berpindah kepada bank lain, serta kurangnya pengetahuan masayarakat pedesaan untuk mengoperasikan Fintech. Abstract The purpose of this research is to find out the opportunities and challenges of fintech in the Islamic banking industry in the midst of a pandemic. This study uses a qualitative descriptive. The object of study in this research is in the form of texts that describe the opportunities and challenges of fintech in the Islamic banking industry. The results of the study show that the Covid-19 pandemic has provided greater opportunities for Islamic banking fintech because the pandemic has encouraged people to carry out e-commerce transactions. The volume of digital banking transactions increased during the pandemic by up to 20.8%, namely reaching 1,493 million transactions and nominally increasing by 23%, reaching IDR 8,223 trillion. The challenges are the security of data and transactions for users of fintech services, the ease with which customers can switch to other banks, and the lack of knowledge of rural communities to operate Fintech.

The rapid development and large-scale application of artificial intelligence, data mining, big data, and cloud computing have already led to dramatic changes in the ecological conditions of social and economic agents. Under the rapid technological development, traditional commercial banks are facing problems such as insufficient development momentum. Therefore, to accelerate its digital transformation, financial technology (fintech) has prompted the banking industry, so as to keep up with the development trend of the times and empower the innovation of commercial banks. Specifically, by analysing the current situation and the impact of the relevant major fintech on the development of the banking industry, this paper aims to gain insight into the advantages and directions of the transformation. The final conclusion of this paper is that, currently, all regions are spending more money on investing in the fintech industry. However, the underlying technological strengths are unevenly developed, with Europe and the US being the most prominent and the Asia-Pacific region catching behind. Fintech represented by artificial intelligence, big data, and cloud computing, can reduce banks' operating costs, helping them accurately profile their customers and intelligently do marketing.

data.Documented value: FinTech Disruption, Retail Banking Dynamics, and Digital Financial Assets: A Volatility Spillover and Risk-Adjusted Performance Analysis

This study examines whether financial technology firms transmit or absorb volatility between digital financial assets and traditional retail banking. Existing research treats these domains separately, comparing FinTech with incumbent banks or cryptocurrencies with equities, leaving the three-way structure unexamined. Using 1,321 aligned daily returns from Coinbase's April 2021 listing to July 2026, a balanced tripartite panel is constructed from two FinTech firms, two retail banks, and two digital assets, benchmarked against the S&P 500. Bitcoin's 24-hour calendar is reconciled with equity trading through log-return accumulation, folding 602 weekend sessions into the following trading day and preserving realised variance that truncation would discard. Volatility connectedness is estimated on model-free Garman-Klass realized volatility rather than on fitted GARCH variances, which avoids the generated-regressor fragility that a proxy robustness check shows can otherwise reverse the headline results. Three formal hypotheses were tested. The null of no structural trend in FinTech systematic risk is rejected since Newey-West trend regressions on rolling betas return probability values below .001 for both the platforms. The null hypothesis of no volatility contagion into retail banking is rejected on a stationary panel, yielding a total spillover index of 48.18 per cent, with banking drawing 20.33 per cent of its forecast error variance through FinTech against 3.75 per cent directly from digital assets. The null hypothesis that the intermediary role does not reverse across macro-financial regimes cannot be rejected because FinTech remains a net transmitter in the boom, tightening cycle, and banking crisis alike. Therefore, FinTech operates as a stable amplifying conduit rather than a cushion, transmitting structural repricing at horizons that a daily monitoring dashboard is least able to observe. Risk-adjusted performance inverts the disruption narrative: retail banking returned 15.83 per cent annually against minus 23.18 per cent for fintech. Perimeter regulation should treat FinTech as a systemic-transmission node.

sections.heading: Fintech Opportunities And Challenges In The Sharia Banking Industry In
paragraphs: ### Sponsor Banks, BaaS, and Plugging Digital [[S1|Al-Masharif Jurnal Ilmu Ekonomi dan Keislaman]]

In the realm of fintech, the Islamic banking industry has faced unprecedented challenges and opportunities during the pandemic. This article delves into the intricacies of how fintech has transformed the Islamic banking sector, particularly in the context of the global pandemic. [[S1|Al-Masharif Jurnal Ilmu Ekonomi dan Keislaman]]

The pandemic has significantly impacted the global economy, leading to a surge in e-commerce transactions. This trend has been particularly notable in the Islamic banking industry, where digital banking transactions have increased by 20.8%, reaching 1.493 billion transactions and a nominal increase of 23%, totaling IDR 8.223 trillion. This growth is largely attributed to the increased reliance on digital platforms for transactions, which have become essential during the pandemic. [[S1|Al-Masharif Jurnal Ilmu Ekonomi dan Keislaman]]

However, this rise in digital transactions has also presented several challenges. One of the primary concerns is the security of data and transactions for users of fintech services. As the industry continues to evolve, the need for robust cybersecurity measures becomes even more critical. Additionally, the ease with which customers can switch to other banks poses a significant challenge. This shift in customer preferences can lead to a loss of customer loyalty and trust, which is crucial for maintaining a stable and competitive Islamic banking industry. [[S1|Al-Masharif Jurnal Ilmu Ekonomi dan Keislaman]]

Another challenge is the lack of knowledge among rural communities regarding the use of fintech. This lack of understanding can hinder the adoption of new financial technologies, thereby limiting the potential benefits of digitalization. Furthermore, the regulatory environment surrounding fintech in the Islamic banking sector is still evolving, leading to uncertainties that can deter banks from fully embracing these technologies. [[S1|Al-Masharif Jurnal Ilmu Ekonomi dan Keislaman]]

Despite these challenges, the pandemic has indeed provided opportunities for the Islamic banking industry. The increased reliance on digital platforms has opened up new avenues for growth and innovation. This shift towards digital banking has not only improved transaction efficiency but has also enhanced financial inclusion. By leveraging the power of technology, Islamic banks can better serve their customers and adapt to the changing needs of the market. [[S1|Al-Masharif Jurnal Ilmu Ekonomi dan Keislaman]]

In conclusion, while the pandemic has presented numerous challenges, it has also created opportunities for the Islamic banking industry to embrace digitalization. By addressing the security concerns, enhancing customer education, and navigating the regulatory landscape, the industry can continue to thrive in the digital age. [[S1|Al-Masharif Jurnal Ilmu Ekonomi dan Keislaman]]

sections.heading: Digitalization, Emerging Technologies, and Financial Stability: Challenges and Opportunities for: evidence angle 5
paragraphs: In the rapidly evolving business environment, financial institutions are faced with the challenge of adapting to the demands of differentiated customer preferences and the increasing demand for digitalization and technological change. This article, based on the research index "Digitalization, Emerging Technologies, and Financial Stability: Challenges and Opportunities for the Indonesian Banking Sector and Beyond" by Muyanja Ssenyonga Jameaba, explores the implications of API-based open banking, Block Chain Technology (BCT), and the entrance of Fintechs, Big technology companies (Big Tech), and Telecommunications companies (Telcos) on the performance of the general banking sector and financial system stability. [[S5|OpenAlex research index]]

The article employs a documentary analysis approach to navigate the ramifications of these technologies on the financial service development and delivery. It highlights the role of digitalization and ICT in fundamentally changing the financial service development and delivery, empowering ICT-savvy non-financial institutions, including Fintechs, Telcos, and Big Tech, to become players in the industry. The article underscores the enhancement of financial inclusion, reduction in transaction costs, and the induction of traditional banks to adopt new business models that leverage Big Data and data analytics. [[S5|OpenAlex research index]]

Digitalization has paved the way for the development of agile, adaptive open banking, supporting business models that are financial and supported by collaboration with other providers of financial services, back-end and front-end technologies, diversified customer base, strengthened capacity and capabilities to leverage customer experience, and the development and deployment of financial innovations. This has significantly improved the competitiveness of the financial sector. [[S5|OpenAlex research index]]

However, despite its many benefits, most banks are yet to adopt BCT due to persisting uncertainty surrounding the technology, its adoption, deployment, and operations. BCT adoption has been undermined by a variety of failures of several BCT-based crypto exchanges and assets, limited understanding of BCT business case, regulatory ambiguity, and risk aversion. The adoption of BCT promises improvement in the integrity and authenticity of financial service delivery, reduction in vulnerability to cyber insecurity, decentralized authentication, increased operational efficiency, low compliance cost, shorter onboarding of new product offers and customers, and accelerated development and deployment of new product offers, which should diversify and broaden liability sources and investment portfolios. [[S5|OpenAlex research index]]

Failure to adopt and deploy both business processes and products on BCT poses the danger of empowering new entrants into financial service development and delivery. The reluctance of conventional banks to adopt and deploy both business processes and products on BCT can lead to the empowerment of new entrants into financial service development and delivery, thereby posing a risk to the stability of the financial system. [[S5|OpenAlex research index]]

The article concludes by emphasizing the importance of collaboration between Fintech firms and banks to improve system-wide financial stability while minimizing the negative externalities of disruption and competition. These findings can help regulators, policymakers, academics, and practitioners understand the opportunities and challenges of emerging technologies in the banking industry. [[S5|OpenAlex research index]]

sections.heading: Fintech and its challenge for banking sector
paragraphs: The rapid development of technology has profoundly transformed consumer behavior, impacting various sectors, including the banking industry. This transformation is expected to optimize technology to enhance productivity and performance, particularly in the financial sector. Technology plays a crucial role in easing financial transactions and minimizing costs, making it essential for the banking sector. In the digital age, most individual activities are conducted through technology, including completing financial transactions. Technology also contributes to promoting financial inclusion, ensuring that everyone has access to financial services. [[S7|The Management Journal of Binaniaga]]

The Covid-19 pandemic has further accelerated the digital adoption across different levels, driven by the necessity for social distancing. This study aims to investigate the fintech strategy to enter the financial service sector and how banks respond to the fintech development. This qualitative research utilized depth interviews and content analysis to provide a valid investigation. The findings revealed that fintech is innovative and promotes innovative strategies to enter the financial service industry. Banks have already prepared to compete in the digital age by investing in software, hardware, and even financial technology companies. This strategy is crucial for maintaining competitiveness in the evolving financial landscape. [[S7|The Management Journal of Binaniaga]]

### S10 — Research in International Business and Finance: The Impact of FinTech Innovation on Digital Financial Literacy in Europe [[S7|The Management Journal of Binaniaga]]

In the evolving financial landscape characterized by the proliferation of FinTech and exacerbated by the Covid-19 pandemic, this paper investigates the unexplored relationship between financial, social, and infrastructural factors and the level of digital financial divide (DFD) of customers in Europe. Applying a difference-in-difference model, the study has revealed that innovation in financial services correlates with a reduced DFD, further reinforced by improved digital infrastructure and social progress. However, paradoxically, the post-Covid environment has widened the gap in financially illiterate regions of the EU. Our results hold relevance for policymakers, governments, and supervisory banking authorities, indicating the most effective areas for intervention in lowering the country's DFD, but they could also support banks in the design of tailor-made digitalization strategies. [[S7|The Management Journal of Binaniaga]]

sections.heading: Thematic Analysis of Financial Technology (Fintech) Influence on the Banking
paragraphs: ### Thematic Analysis of Financial Technology (Fintech) Influence on the Banking Industry [[S1|Risks]]

The integration of technology and finance has given rise to the concept of financial technology (Fintech), which has significantly transformed the banking industry. This article aims to explore how Fintech has influenced recent changes in the banking sector and the upcoming challenges it presents. The analysis is based on a comprehensive thematic review of recent studies on Fintech in the banking industry. [[S1|Risks]]

Fintech has the potential to grow and impact the banking industry and the entire world. It offers immense benefits, such as increased efficiency, improved customer experience, and enhanced security measures. However, with these benefits come drawbacks, including increased reliance on technology, high costs, and job losses. The use of emerging technology and collaboration between Fintech firms and banks can mitigate these negative externalities, promoting system-wide financial stability. [[S1|Risks]]

One of the key areas where Fintech is making significant strides is in the realm of blockchain technology. Blockchain, a decentralized and secure ledger system, is being explored for various banking applications, including cross-border payments, smart contracts, and asset-backed lending. This technology not only enhances security but also reduces the need for intermediaries, thereby lowering transaction costs and increasing speed. [[S1|Risks]]

Another area where Fintech is revolutionizing the banking industry is through artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning. These technologies are being used to automate various banking processes, from customer service to risk assessment. This not only improves customer satisfaction but also reduces the need for human intervention, leading to lower operational costs. [[S1|Risks]]

However, the adoption of Fintech also poses challenges. The increased reliance on technology can lead to a higher dependency on technology, which may not always be reliable or secure. Additionally, the high costs associated with implementing Fintech solutions can be a significant barrier for smaller banks. Furthermore, the rise of Fintech firms has led to job losses in traditional banking sectors, particularly in roles that require human interaction and customer service. [[S1|Risks]]

Despite these challenges, the potential benefits of Fintech outweigh the drawbacks. The use of emerging technology and collaboration between Fintech firms and banks can help mitigate these challenges, promoting a more stable and efficient banking system. This can be particularly beneficial for regulators, policymakers, academics, and practitioners, who can better understand the opportunities and challenges of emerging technologies in the banking industry. [[S1|Risks]]

In conclusion, while the integration of Fintech presents both opportunities and challenges, the potential benefits of this technology far outweigh the drawbacks. As the banking industry continues to evolve, it is essential to address these challenges and harness the opportunities presented by Fintech to ensure a more stable and efficient financial system. [[S1|Risks]]

sections.heading: Evidence angle 9: market scope and limits
paragraphs: In the digital (R)Evolution of the German Banking Sector, the influence of FinTech companies and innovations is becoming increasingly significant. The rapid advancements in artificial intelligence, data mining, big data, and cloud computing have led to substantial changes in the ecological conditions of social and economic agents. Traditional commercial banks are grappling with issues such as insufficient development momentum, necessitating a digital transformation to keep pace with the times. This transformation has been prompted by financial technology (fintech), which has spurred the banking industry to innovate and empower commercial banks. [[S2|Business and Management Research]]

The article investigates the role of FinTech companies and innovations in the German banking sector, focusing on the topic of robo-advice. Robo-advisors, defined as digital platforms that provide automated, algorithm-driven financial planning services with minimal human supervision, are becoming more relevant as consumer behavior and customer needs evolve. This shift towards digital investment advisory services is a potential alternative to conventional asset management, offering convenience and accessibility without the need for human oversight. [[S2|Business and Management Research]]

FinTech companies and innovations have a significant impact on the German banking sector, particularly in the realm of robo-advisory. These companies leverage advanced technologies to provide personalized financial advice, making complex financial decisions more accessible to a broader audience. The influence of FinTech companies extends beyond just robo-advisory, encompassing various aspects of the banking industry, including digital banking, mobile payments, and online banking services. [[S2|Business and Management Research]]

The article emphasizes the importance of understanding the limits of this market scope. While the potential for innovation and growth in the FinTech sector is vast, the implementation of these technologies must be carefully considered. The German banking sector faces challenges in terms of regulatory compliance, customer trust, and the integration of new technologies into existing systems. These factors limit the extent to which FinTech can fully transform the industry. [[S2|Business and Management Research]]

The article also highlights the uneven development of technological strengths across different regions. While Europe and the US are leading in the adoption of fintech innovations, the Asia-Pacific region is catching up. This regional disparity underscores the need for a balanced approach to the integration of FinTech into the banking sector, ensuring that all regions can benefit from the advancements in technology. [[S2|Business and Management Research]]

In conclusion, the article underscores the significant role of FinTech companies and innovations in the German banking sector, particularly in the context of robo-advisory. While the potential for growth and innovation is substantial, the implementation of these technologies must be carefully managed to ensure that the benefits are maximized without compromising the stability and security of the banking system. [[S2|Business and Management Research]]

### FinTech Disruption, Retail Banking Dynamics, and Digital Financial Assets: A Volatility Spillover and Risk-Adjusted Performance Analysis [[S3|Research in International Business and Finance]]

This study examines whether financial technology firms transmit or absorb volatility between digital financial assets and traditional retail banking. Existing research treats these domains separately, comparing FinTech with incumbent banks or cryptocurrencies with equities, leaving the three-way structure unexamined. Using 1,321 aligned daily returns from Coinbase's April 2021 listing to July 2026, a balanced tripartite panel is constructed from two FinTech firms, two retail banks, and two digital assets, benchmarked against the S&P 500. Bitcoin's 24-hour calendar is reconciled with equity trading through log-return accumulation, folding 602 weekend sessions into the following trading day and preserving realised variance that truncation would discard. Volatility connectedness is estimated on model-free Garman-Klass realized volatility rather than on fitted GARCH variances, which avoids the generated-regressor fragility that a proxy robustness check shows can otherwise reverse the headline results. Three formal hypotheses were tested. The null of no structural trend in FinTech systematic risk is rejected since Newey-West trend regressions on rolling betas return probability values below .001 for both the platforms. The null hypothesis of no volatility contagion into retail banking is rejected on a stationary panel, yielding a total spillover index of 48.18 per cent, with banking drawing 20.33 per cent of its forecast error variance through FinTech against 3.75 per cent directly from digital assets. The null hypothesis that the intermediary role does not reverse across macro-financial regimes cannot be rejected because FinTech remains a net transmitter in the boom, tightening cycle, and banking crisis alike. Therefore, FinTech operates as a stable amplifying conduit rather than a cushion, transmitting structural repricing at horizons that a daily monitoring dashboard is least able to observe. Risk-adjusted performance inverts the disruption narrative: retail banking returned 15.83 per cent annually against minus 23.18 per cent for fintech. Perimeter regulation should treat FinTech as a systemic-transmission node. [[S3|Research in International Business and Finance]]
